_comment: Each entry waives one baseline line that no longer exists anywhere in the skill tree. Replace every REASON with why losing this line is safe. Editing the line's wording changes its hash and revokes the waiver.

waived.00bbd60131510c5b: Rewritten in place, not deleted. The sentence '**When the gate says clean and the pixels say broken, the PIXELS win.**' still opens the replacement paragraph, word for word. Only the clause after it changed, because the reason it is true changed.
waived.177ecdff8385248a: The claim survives, restated. Paint order is still named as the fault class that keeps proving the rule. The old wording said the lint 'does not model paint order' as an absolute, and that is now false: OCCLUSION, RULE THROUGH TEXT and TEXT NOT VISIBLE all reason about it. Leaving the absolute in place would teach a limit the tool no longer has.
waived.2c153eb8875646a6: The measurement it carried is preserved and extended. The footer-hairline-over-a-sources-line case is still cited by name, now beside the two further real decks that proved the same class: a 150-tile field erasing a caption, and a dashed rule of 40 boxes struck through a footnote.
waived.ec03c69ba6a39f22: Same content, made useful. OCCLUSION and RULE THROUGH TEXT are still named, but no longer described only as 'two new hard checks' — the replacement says WHAT changed about them (coverage is now measured as a union, so something assembled from many small parts cannot slip a per-shape threshold), which is the part a reader needs in order to generalise.
waived.8494159648662c1a: Extended in place, nothing dropped. The item gained a second half (name the anchor of every label, list the slides) and so gained a word in its title, which is what changed the hash.
waived.e25e602954d2742b: The 'a net, not a proof' caveat is kept verbatim in the replacement. The sentence it belonged to now also introduces TEXT NOT VISIBLE and, more importantly, the reason the old design failed: it enumerated CAUSES, which are unbounded, instead of measuring the effect. That rationale is the generalisable lesson and did not exist in the baseline.

The 'plain text line offering yes / no / other; never fake a form' instruction and the whole 'The ordering is the point' clause survive verbatim; what was inserted between them is the new rule that each answer must be spelled out by what it DOES. waived.b8e71271d0c5de70: Reworded, not deleted: '**yes — update first.**' became '**yes — update to the latest GitHub version first, then build the whole deck on it.**' Same option, same action, same following command list. 'yes' alone read as vague assent and never said WHAT is updated to WHAT; the deck-wide consequence was stated two paragraphs later and nowhere on the option itself.
waived.2d4dbde9a1aaf772: Reworded, not deleted: '**no — build on the installed version.**' became '**no — don't update; build on the installed version.**' The mid-project rationale after it is byte-identical. The added clause fixes a real ambiguity — a bare 'no' reads as declining the question rather than as declining THE UPDATE, which is the one thing a user must understand before answering.
waived.3c5e27bcc4304302: Extended in place, not deleted. The build -> render -> lint chain is byte-identical except that `render_deck.sh <deck>.pptx` gained ` --fast`. The advice to use --fast on fix rounds already stood one paragraph above this command and was omitted FROM it, which is the same as absent: the chain is what gets copied every round, the paragraph is not. Safe unconditionally — with no cache --fast prints `fell back to a full render: no previous render cache` and does the full one. The `--deliverables` carve is stated on the new lines that follow.
waived.c07634c78f790aa4: Deleted because it was FALSE. The cell claimed CJK_NO_EA is what catches you if you skip references/deck-setup.md on a non-16:9 surface or a supplied template. CJK_NO_EA fires only on CJK runs missing an <a:ea> font — it has nothing to do with canvas format or with templates, and on a Latin 4:3 deck it cannot fire at all. A backstop column that names a gate which cannot run is worse than an empty cell: it reads as covered. The replacement says which branch each gate really holds (CJK only) and states plainly that the non-16:9 and template branches have no gate of their own, naming the human step upstream that does hold them.
waived.7c5f620d0b50e6a3: Deleted because the measurement inverted. '~5s vs ~12s full' was true before the render optimizations; re-measured on the current code, --slides 6 costs ~2.9s against ~2.8s for a full 18-slide render — one page is now marginally SLOWER, because a fixed ~2.5s LibreOffice start dominates and page count barely moves it. Restating the old ratio would sell --slides as a speed flag it is not. The replacement keeps the byte-identical-evidence claim (still true and still the point) and relocates the saving to where it actually is: authoring one slide instead of twenty.
waived.fd536d8bfb46c047: Same inverted measurement as baseline:760, in the parenthetical that carried the numbers. 'build ≈ 1.8s, --slides ≈ 4.7s vs 12.3s full' is stale in all three figures. The replacement gives the re-measured pair (≈2.9s vs ≈2.8s), explains WHY they are equal (one fixed LibreOffice start), and keeps every non-numeric claim the sentence made: cheaper than a critic round, spent before the expensive authoring, one build script not two, and the asset note.
waived.fd61ef53fe12c1e9: Not deleted — RE-WRAPPED. This is one physical line holding the tail of the CJK_NO_EA clause and the whole OLDSTYLE_FIGURES clause. The CJK_NO_EA half was extended (it now names retrofit_ea as the fix for the deck in hand), which lengthened the prefix; every word of the OLDSTYLE_FIGURES half is present verbatim on the new line, including 'digits at mixed heights make a big number visibly bob', deckkit.numeral_run_face, and 'a taste call, deliberately not a build blocker'. A line-keyed checker cannot see that, which is what this waiver records.
waived.d0cc1d7656404cbb: Deleted because the numbers are stale. Re-measured on the current code, an 18-slide full render is ~2.8s (not ~12s) and a one-slide --fast round ~2.3s (not ~4.7s). The replacement carries the new figures AND the conclusion the old ones hid: the no-op round is the big win because it never starts LibreOffice, while a one-slide round still pays the ~2.5s start and saves about a fifth. Keeping '~12s' would have kept teaching that rendering is expensive enough to skip.
waived.fb6ccf4017be35c4: Same stale-benchmark sentence as baseline:1350, continued across the line break. The two claims it carried both survive in the replacement: the no-change run costs 0.07s, and --fast output is byte-identical to a full render (verified), so the critic and the render-time lint see exactly what they would have seen anyway.
waived.f8c1f665bd175fbf: Deleted because it was FALSE about its own tool. It said to run --record 'on every round' and that 'rounds is the count of distinct reviews recorded'. validate_review.py --record writes reviews_seen, never rounds: it PRESERVES a rounds that is already there and derives none, because nothing inside a review file says which round it belongs to. The replacement says run it on every REVIEW, names reviews_seen, gives the 2-lens x 2-round example that records 4, and flags rounds as the one hand-typed field in the block. Every surviving clause of the old sentence (moved/edited/revise-verdict reviews fail the hand-off) is kept.
waived.b56ec6f0c8bb2cdd: Same false claim as baseline:1702, continued across the line break — 'so it cannot be inflated' was the load-bearing half, and it is exactly backwards for a field the tool never computes. The trailing clause it shared the line with ('On a high-stakes deck, --record on the arbiter's Job-2 payload files the corroborating pass under critic.corroborated_by') is preserved verbatim.
waived.b19fed965cff07ac: Deleted because the enumeration was incomplete. render_deck.py accepts a FIFTH critic waiver category, cap-reached-majors-open, and this JSON template listed only four — so the file that ACCEPTED it told every reader it did not exist. That is not cosmetic: the missing one is the only honest label for a loop that RAN to its cap with majors open, and its absence steered authors to user-waived, a claim about a conversation that did not happen. The replacement lists all five.
waived.e935eff1e5ff6808: Same incompleteness as baseline:1914, in the prose gloss under the template: 'If none of the four fits' counted a set that had five members. The replacement keeps the external-deck gloss verbatim, adds the cap-reached-majors-open gloss with its two extra required fields (open, surfaced_to_user) and the instruction to prefer it over user-waived whenever the loop ran, and ends with the same sentence updated to five.
